dimensions.note: ssh_key_ref is a sensitive-marked vault reference resolved through the plain-object context.vaultService; the key reaches ssh-agent over stdin, never argv, a resource or a log. Vendored _lib/ssh.ts is the canonical ssh-host blob fe0139f0: no content-derived hash on any local argv or remote script text. The revert token is a random correlation id, not a credential (sensitive-field warning accepted with the host-net/server-host comment). Live cell 11: 0 private-key hits in about 2,500 sampled argv lines on both sides, the run log and .swamp/.
Each method logs the host and outcome once; no key material, config text or host keys in log fields. Residual LOW: a no-op apply logs '(token )'.

kea-dhcp4 -t rejection, a busy revert claim, a failed timer arm, a failed config-set and a failed restore are typed SshErrors; a failure after the claim runs the same restore.sh the timer would and disarms only on a pass, otherwise it surfaces recovery.txt. commit refuses after expiry, after a fired revert, on hash drift, on an inactive service and on an unreachable canary. Residual MEDIUMs (r3): the restore lock timeout clears active.json without reverting (fails loud), commit stops the timer before the drift check, commit's enable runs before the lock, and the failed-restore message says 'timer left armed' after active.json is cleared.

73 unit/contract tests: grammar, deterministic render goldens checked by kea-dhcp4 -t when installed, memfile/lease_cmds parsing, the vendored transport, the plain-object context (vaultService object, readResource/writeResource store), arm-before-write ordering, no-op and refusal paths, distinct resource names across apply/leases/get/commit, and a fired revert discarding the pending apply. Host scripts were run under sh -eu in a real Kea container. Residual MEDIUM: no unit test drives commit through a failing gate. Live: 11/11 on <vps1> at fddc66d.

An apply whose rendered sha equals the live file with the service active is a no-op that arms nothing (live 6: no revert dir, no timer, same mtime and MainPID); a second remove is a no-op (live 10). Every change runs under an armed host-side revert that restores the previous config unless committed (live 5: an uncommitted apply reverted after 120 s, client lease back on the original pool). Residuals: the timer fires about 35 s after the recorded expiry; a malformed active.json reads as no revert armed.

ISC Kea 2.4 (distro kea-dhcp4-server 2.4.1, Ubuntu 24.04): config-set with the whole {"Dhcp4": ...} object over the control socket, config-hash-get for verification, kea-dhcp4 -t before any change, memfile CSV leases by default and the lease_cmds hook opt-in. Drift compares the tool's read-back (file sha and Kea's config hash), not the render text. classless-static-route is out of scope for the stock 2.4 option set.

One flock serializes commit and restore; staged files are moved atomically and removed on failure; each revert directory is cleaned on commit or after firing. Residual LOW/MEDIUM: restore.sh copies over the live file non-atomically, prior.json is written but unused, and remove leaves the stock config as root:_kea 0640.

Manifest @randybias/kea-dhcp 2026.10.17.1, two-sentence description, Apache-2.0, additionalFiles README.md and LICENSE.txt. install, apply, commit and remove are actions; render, get, sync and leases are read-only. Leak scan, gitleaks and fixture guard pass; fixtures use RFC 5737 addresses; live receipts in the LOGBOOK redact the host as <vps1>.

Every argument and resource schema is a strictObject; IPv4, CIDR, MAC, interface, FQDN, pools and typed DHCP options carry grammars and bounds, overlapping pools are refused at validation, and an interface carrying the SSH session is refused before staging (live 8). host_keys are required: the transport is strict-only, no insecure_tofu.
config, pending, revert, observation, render and action infinite/10; leases 7d/5.

install, render, apply (create or converge), commit, get, sync, leases and remove. remove is an action that restores the captured stock config under the same arm/verify/commit protocol, so no method tombstones the definition.

Inputs, pools, options and the SSH-interface guard are validated before any change; the rendered config is checked by kea-dhcp4 -t on the host before it is installed (live 7: a Kea-invalid config left file, timers and MainPID unchanged); a lease_cmds hook must live in the discovered hooks dir, root-owned and not writable by others. Host keys are pinned by the canonical transport. The remote user must be root (documented).

Records are keyed by host, port and user: config-<key>, pending-<key>, observation-<key>, leases-<key>, revert-<key>-<token>, <method>-<key> for action outcomes, and render-<sha256>; live round F1 (one name shared by config, observation and leases) is fixed and confirmed live.
Targets, keys and DHCP inputs arrive as method arguments; the model reads back only its own pending, config and revert records.
First publish: no prior stored attributes, so no upgrade entries are needed.
